body:
This feels like a hack, why does it work and what is it solving?

Also, regarding the comment, is it _Windows_ specific or is it _PowerShell_ specific?
Agree, I would like to understand this better.

I looks like right after the calls to git the filesystem state hasn't finished updating yet causing some of the tests to fail ([test run before change](https://github.com/starship/starship/runs/249566711), [test run after change](https://github.com/starship/starship/runs/249783836)). I also added these barriers after each call to git, even where it hadn't caused issues yet, to reduce possible test flakiness. I believe it isn't trivial to start a full fs sync on windows.
This addition is Windows specific though other operating systems could have the same issue. None of the tests cover anything powershell-specific yet.
Ah okay, good to know thanks!

body:
Unsolicited (sorry!) but FWIW, this breaks on my mac when `Get-Job | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'Running' }` returns one or fewer results.

```Suggestion
    $jobs = if ($j = Get-Job | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'Running' }) { $j.Count }
```
or

```Suggestion
    Get-Job | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'Running' } | Measure-Object | Select-Object -Expand Count
```

+#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
+
+# Starship assumes UTF-8
+[Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8
+function global:prompt {
+    $out = $null
+    $jobs = @(Get-Job | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'Running' }).Count
+
+    if ($lastCmd = Get-History -Count 1) {
+        $duration = [math]::Round(($lastCmd.EndExecutionTime - $lastCmd.StartExecutionTime).TotalSeconds)
+        $out = @(&::STARSHIP:: prompt --status=$lastexitcode --jobs=$jobs --cmd-duration=$duration)
+    }
+    else {
+        $out = @(&::STARSHIP:: prompt --status=$lastexitcode --jobs=$jobs)
+    }
+
+    $out -join "`n"
body:
I understand everything in this file except for this line.
What does ``$out -join "`n"`` do here?
Running some tests on another branch, I think we may no longer need this for tests to pass. Might've been solved by an update in `tempfile` or `docker`. Not too sure 🤷‍♂

If it's still needed I think this should be changed to `cfg!(darwin)`
